questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Normal Equation for a Weighted Least-Squares Problem
questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 0 \\ 0 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{3}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}18 & 0 \\ 8 & 4 \\ 8 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}68 & 0 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=68+8+0=76.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Solution to a Weighted Least-Squares Problem
questions.problem:
Find the solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 27 \\ 27\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{5}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}25 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}25 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}25 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 27 \\ 27\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 25 \\ -4 & 0 \\ 4 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 108 \\ 108\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}8 & 4 \\ 4 & 29\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 108\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the matrix on the left-hand side is invertible, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & ={[\begin{aligned}8 & 4 \\ 4 & 29\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 108\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8\cdot 29-4\cdot 4}[\begin{aligned}29 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 108\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{216}[\begin{aligned}-432 \\ 864\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -4 & 4 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -16 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the matrix on the left-hand side is invertible, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & ={[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -10\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9\cdot 8-(-2)\cdot (-2)}[\begin{aligned}8 & 2 \\ 2 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}11 \\ -10\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{68}[\begin{aligned}68 \\ -68\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {3}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 9 & -9 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}22 & -8 \\ -8 & 11\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}14 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the matrix on the left-hand side is invertible, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & ={[\begin{aligned}11 & 8 \\ 8 & 22\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}14 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{11\cdot 22-8\cdot 8}[\begin{aligned}11 & 8 \\ 8 & 22\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}14 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{178}[\begin{aligned}178 \\ 178\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 4 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 9 \\ 9 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{3}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 4 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 27 \\ 16 & -4 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-18 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}77 & 9 \\ 9 & 86\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -56\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=77+86+(-56)=107.
$$
